issues.legal_issue: Prior permission for regulated-area development is not required merely to initiate land acquisition for a statutory scheme intended to secure regulated development.
material_facts: The land proposed for acquisition was in a regulated area.
The acquisition was initiated for a statutory land-development scheme framed by a public board for regulated development.
The physical development activities governed by the general building-control law had not begun.
issues.conclusion: The absence of prior permission under the general building-control law did not make the acquisition proceedings ultra vires.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the U.P. (Regulation of Building Operations) Act, 1958 governs development activities, not proceedings to acquire land for a scheme that may later lead to those activities. The U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965 is a self-contained special Act; in the absence of a provision making its schemes subject to the general Act, its provisions prevail. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: scheme_acquisition_challenge and regulated_area and prior_permission_objection and scheme_for_regulated_development and physical_development_not_started

predicates.scheme_acquisition_challenge: The case challenges land-acquisition proceedings initiated to carry out a statutory housing or improvement scheme.
predicates.regulated_area: The land proposed for acquisition lies in an area subject to regulation of building operations.
predicates.prior_permission_objection: The challenger argues that prior permission for development was not obtained.
predicates.scheme_for_regulated_development: A public body framed the scheme for the purpose of regulated development.
predicates.physical_development_not_started: The physical site or building activities governed by the general development rules had not begun.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns acquisition for a regulated-development scheme and the regulated physical work has not begun, the missing development permission does not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to sanction a statutory scheme within the stated six-month period does not, by itself, make the scheme invalid.
material_facts: The board received objections to the scheme and heard the objectors.
The scheme was sanctioned more than six months after the objections were received.
The governing scheme provision stated that the board may, so far as may be, act within six months.
issues.conclusion: The six-month period was directory, not mandatory, and the scheme was valid despite the delay.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31 of the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965 states that the board may, so far as may be, act within six months after receipt of the last objection. The Court construed that qualified language as making the period directory rather than an absolute limit. It cited no earlier cases.

predicates.statutory_scheme_challenge: The case challenges the validity of a scheme framed under a statutory housing or improvement scheme process.
predicates.objections_received: Objections to the scheme were received by the responsible board.
predicates.sanction_after_stated_period: The scheme was sanctioned after the framework's stated period for sanction had elapsed.

issues.definition: If a statutory scheme is sanctioned after the stated period following receipt of objections, the delay alone does not invalidate it.

issues.legal_issue: The decision whether urgency justifies taking possession of waste or arable land before an award is for the appropriate government.
material_facts: The government invoked the urgent-possession procedure before an award was made.
The challenge disputed whether the circumstances warranted urgency.
issues.conclusion: Whether urgency existed was left to the discretion and decision of the appropriate government.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 leaves it to the appropriate government's discretion in cases of urgency to direct possession of waste or arable land needed for public purposes before an award is made. Section 17(4) permits the government, where the relevant urgency provisions apply in its opinion, to direct that the Section 5A inquiry not apply. The Court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.urgent_acquisition_challenge: The case challenges an acquisition in which possession is sought before an award on grounds of urgency.
predicates.land_is_arable: The land subject to acquisition is arable land.
predicates.government_invoked_urgent_possession: The appropriate government directed that possession be taken under an urgent-possession process.

issues.definition: In a challenge to urgent possession of arable land before an award, the urgency determination is left to the appropriate government.

issues.legal_issue: A Section 5A inquiry does not apply to land proposed to be acquired under a notified statutory housing or improvement scheme.
material_facts: The land was proposed to be acquired under a housing or improvement scheme notified under the special Act.
The special Act modified the Land Acquisition Act to make Section 5A inapplicable to land proposed to be acquired under such a notified scheme.
issues.conclusion: The Section 5A inquiry was inapplicable to the acquisition under the notified scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Section 55 of the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965 modified the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 by making Section 5A inapplicable to land proposed to be acquired under specified notified housing or improvement schemes. The Court treated this as an express legislative decision to dispense with that inquiry for such schemes. It cited no earlier cases.

predicates.notified_scheme_acquisition: The land is proposed to be acquired under a notified statutory housing or improvement scheme.

issues.definition: When land is proposed to be acquired under a notified statutory housing or improvement scheme, the inquiry otherwise available to landowners is not required.

issues.legal_issue: An unconsidered representation under the scheme-review process does not bar urgent possession where the government itself sanctioned the scheme.
material_facts: The appellants had made representations to the government concerning the scheme.
The government sanctioned the scheme itself.
The appellants argued that urgent acquisition should not proceed before their representation was considered.
issues.conclusion: The scheme-review power had no relevance to the power to take possession under the urgent-possession provision, and there was no room for the review power where the government itself had sanctioned the scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49 of the U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad Adhiniyam, 1965 empowers the government to call for and examine the board's scheme records and to modify, annul, or remit a scheme for reconsideration. That power does not affect the urgent-possession power under Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; where the government itself sanctioned the scheme, there is no scope for exercising the Section 49 review power. The Court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.urgent_acquisition_challenge: The case challenges urgent possession in an acquisition undertaken for a statutory housing or improvement scheme.
predicates.scheme_representation_unconsidered: A representation about the scheme had been made to the government but had not been considered before the urgent-possession step.
predicates.government_sanctioned_scheme: The government itself sanctioned the scheme.

issues.definition: When the government itself sanctioned a scheme, an unconsidered representation about that scheme does not bar urgent possession in an acquisition for it.
